case_data.title: Faust-Shop Participatory Arts Performance
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
In 2025, an academic research team initiated a process that used participatory arts, including multimedia documentary theatre and a long table discussion, to involve approximately 20 people in an interactive performance lecture to examine the interaction between humans and AI with the intended outcomes of building participant capacity to engage with AI and creating re-usable participation tools and methods.

This project brought together stakeholder groups that usually don’t share their attitudes to AI. This included voice and movement artists, actors, leaders from the private and public sectors, students, organisational consultants, technologists. It also, for the first time, introduced artistic research and performance based approach to the British Computer Society events series.
case_data.what-limitations-to-the-project-should-b: This was a ticketed event in London with a small ticket price.
case_data.why-is-this-project-important-to-include: This project brought together stakeholder groups that usually don’t share their attitudes to AI. This included voice and movement artists, actors, leaders from the private and public sectors, students, organisational consultants, technologists. It also for the first time introduced artistic research and performance based approach to the British Computer Society events series. I used this project as a case study for my certification as organisational consultant using a systems psychodynamics approach.
project-goals: Methods: Create re-usable participation tools & methods
Capacity: Build participant capacity to engage with AI
case_data.describe-the-subject-matter-in-your-own-: Human-AI systems: the interaction between humans and AI
